qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Long-dated hydroelectric concessions along the Danube and Austrian Alps with run-of-river and pumped-storage plants operating at the bottom of the European merit order. Strong historical 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 21.0% driven by zero-fuel-cost hydro generation, though earnings are exposed to wholesale merchant power price volatility and statutory windfall profit taxes.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (gate_6 = N, REJECT). Austria's dominant hydroelectric generator possessing irreplaceable dam concessions, but fails Gate 6 Pillar 1 peak-to-peak earnings power compounding. Record FY2023 earnings (€6.52 Owner EPS) represented an unrepeatable energy crisis windfall spike; earnings have collapsed significantly as European wholesale power prices normalized (€4.29 Owner EPS in FY2025). Furthermore, Austria has extended statutory windfall taxes on inframarginal hydro through 2030, capping upside while downside volume risk (droughts) remains unhedged.
qualitative.evidence: While Verbund maintains a low-leverage balance sheet (Net Debt/NI of 1.04x) and strong multi-year GAAP ROIC (21.0% median), its earnings fail Gate 6 Pillar 1. FY2023 net income of €2.27B and EPS of €6.52 were driven by historical European energy crisis gas and power price spikes. As wholesale power prices normalized, net income contracted by 34% to €1.49B (€4.29 EPS) in FY2025. Austrian statutory extension of the Energy Crisis Contribution (windfall tax) through 2030 permanently skims supernormal profits, leaving the company exposed to commodity power swings and weather volatility without secular peak-to-peak compounding.
